transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess mostly it’s my sleep, doctor. It’s not terrible all the time, but… I don’t sleep right anymore. I’ll lie there a long while, and then if I do doze off, I wake up from bad dreams or just little noises. After that I can’t seem to settle back down. I thought maybe I ought to come in and ask about it, if that’s alright.
Have you experienced or witnessed any traumatic events recently or in the past that still affect you emotionally?

I’m not sure I’d call anything that, doctor. I mean, I’ve seen some hard things over the years, like most folks my age, but nothing I can point to and say, “that’s the thing.” I don’t want to make too much of it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you ever find yourself thinking about or re-experiencing any past events in a way that feels intrusive or upsetting, even if you don’t consider them traumatic?

Well… yes, I suppose sometimes. I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is, but if I hear metal scrape, or I see a ladder leaning up in somebody’s yard, it can sort of… jump right back into my head. Like I’m under there again, waiting for help. It passes, usually, but it does shake me some. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?

When you have these reactions to things like a ladder or metal scraping, do you find that these situations cause you to avoid certain places or activities, or do you generally feel okay when those things aren’t around?

I’d like to say I’m generally fine when they’re not around… and mostly I am, I think. But I guess I do find myself making excuses sometimes. I’ll tell myself I’m too tired to go to the senior center, or that the garage can wait.

And, well, I don’t much like working near the tools anymore, especially over by where I used to keep that ladder. I don’t know if that counts as avoiding exactly, but I suppose I do steer clear of it more than I used to.
Do you find yourself feeling on edge, irritable, or unusually down more often than not, especially when these memories come up?

I wouldn’t say I’m angry all the time, no… but I do get a little short with people over things that don’t really matter. Like if my wife moves something in the garage, I might snap at her before I even think about it.

Then afterward I feel bad, because she didn’t do anything wrong. I don’t like being that way.
Do you often feel a lasting sense of guilt, anger, or fear connected to those memories that come back, even when you're not actively thinking about them?

I don’t know if I’d call it guilt exactly… maybe fear, more than anything. And I know this may sound foolish, Doctor, but since then I keep thinking ordinary things aren’t as safe as they look.

Like, if I trust something simple, it might just… turn on me. I tell myself that’s not reasonable, but the thought stays around more than I’d like. Does that make sense?
Do you find that these feelings of fear or unease stick with you even when you're not thinking about those memories, like a background worry that doesn’t go away?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. Not every minute, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but there’s this sort of worry sitting in the back of my mind.

I know it may sound foolish, Doctor, but now I catch myself thinking everyday things aren’t as safe as they look. Like if I trust something simple, it could turn on me somehow. I know that probably doesn’t make much sense, but that feeling does hang around.
Do you find that these feelings of fear or unease stick with you even when you're not thinking about those memories, like a background worry that doesn’t go away?

Yes, sir… I suppose it does. Not like I’m terrified all day or anything, but there’s this little thought that sticks around.

I know it may sound foolish, but I keep thinking everyday things aren’t as safe as they look. Like if I trust something simple, it could sort of turn on me. I know that doesn’t sound very reasonable, but that’s the worry that sits there.
Do you find yourself getting easily startled or unusually watchful, like you're always on the lookout for something going wrong, even in safe or ordinary situations?

Yes… a little, I suppose. I don’t mean I’m acting jumpy all the time, Doctor, but when I go places now, I do tend to look around first.

I’ll notice what might fall, where the exits are, whether the floor or the steps look steady… things like that. Once I’ve checked it over a bit, then I can sit easier. I hope that’s the kind of thing you mean.
